incidents.victim: Global critical infrastructure and government agencies
incidents.attacker: China — state-linked espionage group (Integrity Technology Group)
incidents.vector: Actors combined automated vulnerability scanning with manual intrusion to target internet-facing systems across government, healthcare, manufacturing, and critical infrastructure sectors globally.
incidents.impact: Five-nation joint advisory AA26-281A issued Oct 8 by FBI, NSA, CISA, UK NCSC, and Australian ACSC; victims span North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific; Integrity Technology Group confirmed to have ties to the Chinese government.

incidents.vector: AI-automated ARTEX (Automated Reconnaissance and Targeted Exploitation) framework identified and exploited vulnerabilities in loan processing and mobile banking systems, exfiltrating customer financial data.
incidents.impact: Multiple South Korean banks and lenders breached; customer financial records exfiltrated; represents one of the first confirmed operational deployments of an AI-automated attack chain against banking infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Global Fortinet VPN and firewall users
incidents.vector: Attackers exploit Fortinet FortiGate credential vulnerabilities to authenticate, create unauthorized admin accounts, and lock out legitimate users; compromised access sold to ransomware affiliates including INC/Lynx and Payload.
incidents.impact: 86,644+ devices confirmed compromised across 194 countries; broader campaign estimated at 400,000–450,000 targeted devices; FBI and U.S. Secret Service issued joint advisory Oct 6 warning organizations of imminent ransomware deployment risk.

incidents.vector: Employee credentials compromised and used to access a Snowflake cloud instance and integrated marketing SaaS platforms; attackers then abused push notification permissions to send malicious messages directly to 17 million customers.
incidents.impact: 17 million customer records exposed; malicious push notifications sent to all ASOS app users; investigation ongoing into full scope of exfiltrated data.

incidents.victim: ATNS — Air Traffic and Navigation Services (South Africa)
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against the operational technology (OT) network of South Africa's state-owned air traffic control and navigation authority.
incidents.impact: Weather and navigation services severely disrupted; air travel across southern Africa near-crippled; OT network compromise raises safety concerns beyond financial impact; recovery ongoing.

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem (axios, Mastra AI, arrayref)
incidents.vector: North Korean actors compromised maintainer accounts for widely-used npm packages (axios, 19M weekly downloads) and Rust crates (arrayref), injecting malicious code designed to steal cloud IAM credentials; used Web3 blockchain infrastructure for covert command and control.
incidents.impact: Malicious versions published to public package registries before detection; cloud environments of any developer who updated affected packages exposed to IAM credential theft; multiple packages unpublished; enables further lateral movement into victim cloud environments.

incidents.victim: DIVD — Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure
incidents.vector: Organization breached by what researchers believe was an autonomous AI agent operating without direct human oversight, using automated vulnerability identification and exploitation techniques.
incidents.impact: Dutch cybersecurity nonprofit systems compromised; incident is among the first confirmed cases of an autonomous AI-driven intrusion; raising significant legal and policy questions about liability for AI agent attacks.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — financial fraud (Tren de Aragua)
incidents.vector: Venezuelan criminal organization Tren de Aragua deployed ATM jackpotting malware at U.S. bank ATM locations, forcing machines to dispense large volumes of cash.
incidents.impact: $40.73 million stolen from U.S. banks; OFAC sanctioned 10 individuals and entities on Sep 30; Tren de Aragua designated as a Specially Designated Narcotics Trafficker.

incidents.vector: Exploited unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability CVE-2026-35273 via an Accenture contractor system; defaced the FBI jobs portal and exfiltrated employee records.
incidents.impact: Sensitive records on nearly all FBI employees stolen, including medical records, home addresses, phone numbers, and task force affiliations; multiple ShinyHunters members arrested in response; FBI disrupted group's infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Three zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-88771 CVSS 9.5, CVE-2026-88772, CVE-2026-88779) exploited in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway; attackers deployed web shells, stole credentials, and conducted internal reconnaissance via novel tunneler malware.
incidents.impact: Exploitation undetected for at least three weeks; dozens of organizations compromised across government, financial services, education, and telecom in North America and Europe; Australian organizations confirmed impacted; 50,000+ vulnerable instances identified.

incidents.victim: Danish government — CPR Civil Registration System
incidents.vector: Unauthorized or abusive access to the Danish Civil Registration System (CPR) by individual(s) with privileged database access; exact mechanism not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Records of all 8 million Danish citizens potentially accessed; incident under investigation by Danish authorities; full scope of data access and attacker identity not yet determined.

incidents.vector: Warlock ransomware group targeted organizations in Spain and Portugal via unspecified initial access vectors; encrypted systems and exfiltrated data across multiple sectors.
incidents.impact: Four confirmed victims: a water utility, a telecom provider, a regional government, and a university; data encryption and exfiltration reported; campaign active over at least two months.

incidents.victim: Medyc and MyDr — Polish healthcare platforms
incidents.vector: Criminal group dubbed 'Fingerprint' breached two major Polish healthcare appointment and records platforms through unspecified initial access, exfiltrating patient records from both.
incidents.impact: 24 million patient records compromised: 5 million from Medyc and 19 million from MyDr; largest healthcare data breach in Polish history; sensitive patient health data exposed.

incidents.victim: Pentagon DMDC — Defense Manpower Data Center
incidents.vector: Unencrypted file-sharing server exposed to the public internet allowed unauthorized access; attackers maintained persistent access for approximately 9 months before detection in July 2026.
incidents.impact: 3.1 million current and former U.S. military personnel records compromised; sensitive personnel data including service records exposed; breach lasted from October 2025 to July 2026.

incidents.vector: Social engineering attack gained unauthorized access to third-party-hosted business applications between June 3–8; attackers exfiltrated patient data and issued a ransom demand.
incidents.impact: 360,000+ patients affected across Texas, South Carolina, and California; health data including insurance numbers, device serial numbers, and dates of service stolen; ransom demanded but no evidence of identity theft use reported.

incidents.vector: Hot wallet compromise through unspecified means resulting in unauthorized large-scale cryptocurrency withdrawals before exchange security systems intervened.
incidents.impact: $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen; largest single cryptocurrency theft of 2026; exchange operations disrupted during incident response and recovery.

incidents.vector: Fake Dubai Airports recruitment lures delivered ShelbyLoader V2 malware; GitHub repositories used as covert command-and-control channel via hidden repository instructions; tunneling malware maintained persistent encrypted access.
incidents.impact: Multiple Iraqi critical infrastructure organizations compromised; sensitive data exfiltrated; campaign (tracked as Blinder Tunnel) attributed to Iran-aligned state actors by Palo Alto Unit 42 with moderate confidence.

incidents.vector: AI-generated deepfake voice calls impersonated the bank's CEO and a lawyer to authorize fraudulent wire transfers totaling €95 million to accounts in China and Hong Kong.
incidents.impact: €95 million transferred; approximately €36 million remains unrecovered; funds routed through Chinese and Hong Kong accounts; case highlights the growing threat of AI voice cloning against financial executives.

incidents.vector: Hacktivist group gained administrator-level access to Moscow's Department of Health network; maintained access for months collecting intelligence on sensitive medical data.
incidents.impact: Sensitive medical data from Moscow's health network accessed; group states data includes Russian military medical records useful for assessing casualties in Ukraine; breach originally occurred in 2023 and was publicly disclosed in October 2026.
